texto: # Prison Break AI A local-first, browser-based multi-agent simulation where agents use deterministic planning (A* pathfinder) with optional one-time LLM-assisted planning to escape procedurally generated mazes. Built as an experiment to explore combining lightweight pathfinding with local LLM planners and physics-based agent simulation. --- ## Live (local) demo ![prison-break-ai](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82a792e6-d371-406c-a277-dc78992ea5ab) Run locally: ```bash npm install npm run dev # then open http://localhost:3000 (or the port printed by Vite) ``` --- ## What this project is - A React + TypeScript front-end using Vite. - Matter.js powers the physics simulation (agents, walls, hazards, exit sensor). - Agents compute full path plans via a local A* pathfinder and follow waypoints. - Optional: call a local Ollama-compatible LLM (via a devproxy `/api/ollama`) to request a one-time longer-horizon plan; this runs in the background and may replace local plans if shorter. - HUD allows toggling walls, trails, obstacles, seeds, and per-agent model selection. The project is intentionally local-first: the Ollama calls are proxied through the dev server to avoid CORS, and the client gracefully falls back to local planning when no LLM is available. --- ## Key features - Procedural maze generation (recursive backtracker). - Deterministic A* pathfinder for reliable planning. - Agents follow full path plans to reduce continual LLM traffic. - Background AI planner (one-time) to optionally improve local plans. - Stall detection and auto-replan (local first, then AI fallback). - HUD with per-agent model selection and runtime diagnostics. - DOM overlay markers that render emoji faces for agents (for easy visual scanning). --- ## Technologies - React + TypeScript + Vite - Matter.js (physics) - Ollama-compatible local LLM (optional) — proxied via Vite dev server - motion (motion/react) + lucide-react for UI affordances --- ## Project structure (important files) - `src/App.tsx` — application orchestration: world creation, agent lifecycle, model probing, plan orchestration. - `src/agents/agent.ts` — `Agent` class: physics body, plan following, stall detection, and optional LLM decision fallback. - `src/ai/client.ts` — centralized LLM client: probe, cached availability check, `getPlanFromAI()` wrapper. - `src/physics/maze.ts` — maze generator (recursive backtracker) and helper data structures. - `src/physics/pathfinder.ts` — grid-based A* pathfinder that returns world-space waypoints. - `src/physics/world.ts` — Matter.js world creation, render plugin for drawing trails and plans. - `src/components/HUD.tsx` — controls for options and per-agent model selection. --- ## Example snippets Agent plan assignment and follow (excerpt from `src/agents/agent.ts`): ```ts public setPlan(plan: { x: number; y: number }[]) { this.plan = plan || []; this.planIndex = 0; if (this.plan.length > 0) { this.data.lastReason = `Following plan (${this.plan.length} steps)`; this.data.lastAction = "WAIT"; } // attach to body plugin for rendering if (!this.body.plugin) this.body.plugin = {} as any; (this.body.plugin as any).plan = this.plan; } private followPlan() { if (!this.plan || this.planIndex >= this.plan.length) { this.plan = []; this.planIndex = 0; this.data.lastAction = "WAIT"; return; } const target = this.plan[this.planIndex]; // ...apply small force toward waypoint } ``` Local planner -> start flow (excerpt from `src/App.tsx`): ```ts const computePlansAndStart = async () => { // compute local A* paths for all agents agentsRef.current.forEach(a => { const plan = findPath(mazeRef.current!, a.body.position, mazeRef.current!.exitPos); if (plan && plan.length > 0) a.setPlan(plan); }); // show plans briefly, then start agents await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 250)); agentsRef.current.forEach(a => a.start()); // background one-time AI planning may replace plans later }; ``` LLM planner invocation (excerpt from `src/ai/client.ts`): ```ts // aiClient.getPlanFromAI(mazeRep, startCell, goalCell, modelName?) const aiPath = await aiClient.getPlanFromAI(mazeRep, startCell, goalCell, agent.data.model); // aiPath is a list of grid cells; map to world-space and call agent.setPlan(worldPlan) ``` --- ## Architecture (high-level) Mermaid diagram (in repo): ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Browser UI] --> B[Matter.js World] A --> C[HUD] B --> D[Agents] D --> E[Local A* Pathfinder] D -->|Optional| F[Ollama Planner via /api/ollama] F --> A ``` Key runtime flow: - Start app → create world and maze → spawn agents → compute local plans → agents start moving - If agent stalls → recompute local path; if failing, call LLM planner in background → adopt plan if better --- ## Running and developing - Install dependencies: `npm install` - Run dev server: `npm run dev` - Build: `npm run build` Notes: - The app expects a local Ollama-compatible server only for optional AI planning. When absent, the app uses the deterministic local planner. - Vite dev server proxies `/api/ollama` -> `http://localhost:11434/api` (see `vite.config.ts`) to avoid CORS during development. --- ## Contributing Thanks for considering contributing! A few ideas and guidelines: - How to contribute 1. Fork the repo and create a topic branch. 2. Run `npm install` and `npm run dev`. 3. Write tests where practical (unit tests for maze generator, pathfinder). 4. Submit a pull request with a clear description and screenshots if UI changes. - Suggested features to implement - Multi-level maze with elevators/teleporters. - More agent behaviors (learning via local reward signals, curriculum training). - Networked multiplayer/spectator mode that streams agent telemetry. - Replace emoji overlay with rich avatar sprites + customizable skins. - Export replay / seed sharing URL. - Add a headless runner for automated benchmarking (measure agent success rates across seeds). --- ## License MIT --- If you'd like, I can also open a PR that adds a GitHub Actions workflow to run TypeScript checks and a simple smoke test on pushes.
